title: Interactive batching safeguard visual configurator
creator: Maya Thompson
summary: Design and prototype an interactive visual configurator inside the Redwood Console that lets engineers and PMs compose batching and caching policies with immediate cost/latency simulations and safety guardrails. The UI emphasizes progressive disclosure, explainable recommendations, and a sandboxed simulator so users can see policy impact before saving a rollout.
goals: Surface actionable recommendations for batching and caching based on workload profile and model family
Make guardrails explicit and configurable (e.g., max latency, max token cost, minimum quality thresholds), with clear default safe-presets
Provide a quick simulation sandbox so users can preview cost and latency distributions across a sample traffic trace
Reduce friction for common use-cases with one-click presets while supporting advanced tuning for power users
success_metrics: % of users who apply a recommended preset without engineering support >= 35% within first 6 weeks
Average time to create and preview a batching policy <= 4 minutes in usability test
Reduction in customer support tickets related to batching config by 20% after release
At least 2-3 teams adopt the simulator during initial rollout (tracked by telemetry)
problem_statement: Current batching/caching config screens are form-heavy, lack contextual help about safety trade-offs, and do not let teams preview the real economic or quality impact of a policy. This leads to conservative defaults, support tickets, and missed cost savings.
user_journeys: Platform engineer wants to lower token spend for an embedding-heavy route while keeping 99th percentile latency below 250ms
PM needs to roll out an aggressive batching policy to a dedicated environment but wants to validate quality regressions using a test prompt set first
SRE wants clear rollback guardrails and an easy way to lock a policy across teams
proposed_components: Policy canvas: drag-and-drop tiles for matchers, batching strategies, and caching rules
Cost & latency preview panel: histogram + percentile table + cost delta estimate
Recommendation ribbon: curated presets with short explainers and expected savings/risks
Guardrail slider group: simple controls (max latency, cost cap, min quality) with tooltips
Simulator: run sample trace to visualize token savings, latency changes, and failure modes
Explainability drawer: natural-language rationale for each recommendation and the top contributing signals
accessibility_notes: All interactive controls must be reachable by keyboard and expose ARIA labels
Color choices for histograms must meet AA contrast for key states; provide pattern fills for color-blind users
Simulator animations should be reducible; provide a static summary for screen readers
Tooltips must be focusable and read by screen readers
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates policy canvas with at least 3 tile types (matcher, batching, caching)
Simulator returns a sample estimated cost delta and latency distribution for provided trace in under 2s (mocked data acceptable for prototype)
Recommendation ribbon contains at least 3 curated presets with one-line explainers
Design reviewed by PM and ENG with documented feedback and follow-ups
Accessible annotations for all controls included in handoff artifacts
tradeoffs_considered: Expose many knobs vs progressive disclosure: chose progressive disclosure to reduce cognitive load for new users
Simulation fidelity vs performance: prototype uses sampled traces and heuristics; engineering will evaluate production simulation cost
Presets ease adoption but might encourage misuse: added inline explainers and opt-in advanced mode
engineering_notes: ENG owners: kernel selection and simulation model will require a lightweight simulator endpoint (see ENG-2319)
Simulator UI will accept anonymized sample traces or synthesized traffic to avoid PII; coordinate with Security for trace sanitization
Telemetry events included above; schema to be finalized with analytics team
Consider server-side evaluation job that caches last simulation run per user to avoid repeated compute
research_findings: Usability interviews (n=8) showed that users want immediate cost feedback and concrete recommended presets rather than purely textual guidance
Participants consistently misinterpreted 'batch size' when presented without example traces; adding a quick example reduced confusion
Advanced users prefer an interactive canvas to express combinatorial rules rather than a linear form
review_feedback: Priya Rao (PM, 2025-03-11): Love the presets. Add an explicit 'safe-mode' toggle that enforces conservative rollout defaults for production routes.
Marcus Li (Eng, 2025-03-13): Simulator looks great. We need a clear contract for input traces and a fallback when live traces are unavailable. Also watch out for expensive backend compute.
Samir Patel (Security, 2025-03-14): Ensure trace sampling excludes user PII and link to DLP checklist in handoff.
Design critique (Internal, 2025-03-18): Reword some tooltip copy to avoid technical jargon; add microcopy for rollback consequences
